blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the global tax footprint of a company is an architecture, not an accident. It is the sum of deliberate choices: where entities are based, how profits flow between them, which jurisdictions carry risk, which functions live where, and how the whole structure survives a decade of political change. Each choice has long-term consequences that are very hard to unwind once they are in place.

The senior leader's task is to keep the architecture visible and to review it honestly every few years. A structure that made sense five years ago, under one set of rules and one set of business priorities, may no longer make sense today. The test is not whether it is legal — most of these structures are — but whether it still reflects the company the business is now trying to be.

The best global tax architectures are boring, defensible, and stable. They do not try to be clever, and they do not appear in articles.

items.q: According to the text, the global tax footprint of a company is best described as…
items.why: "the global tax footprint of a company is an architecture, not an accident… the sum of deliberate choices".

items.q: What is described as the real test of a tax structure?
options: Whether it minimises tax in every jurisdiction
Whether it still reflects the company the business is now trying to be
items.why: "The test is not whether it is legal… but whether it still reflects the company the business is now trying to be."

items.q: The author says the best global tax architectures "do not appear in articles." This most likely suggests that…
options: good structures are quiet and unremarkable, not aggressive schemes that make headlines
the press is not interested in tax
articles are an unreliable source of information
items.why: Inferência: aparecer na imprensa costuma significar escândalo/esquema agressivo; o texto valoriza o "chato" e defensável.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Structural choices are very hard to reverse once in place.
Business priorities can drift away from an existing structure.
A tax structure should be reviewed honestly every few years.
A structure that is legal today can safely be left untouched indefinitely.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta o oposto — legalidade não basta, e a arquitetura precisa ser revista com o passar dos anos.

items.q: Why does the text stress that choices are "very hard to unwind once they are in place"?
options: To show that tax structures are illegal
To explain why advisers are expensive
To justify treating the architecture as a long-term, deliberate decision rather than a quick fix
To argue that structures should never be changed
items.why: Inferência: a dificuldade de desfazer é o motivo para decidir com cuidado e revisar honestamente, não para congelar tudo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James conduzindo a revisão da arquitetura tributária no conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. Before we look at a single entity chart, I want to be honest about why we are here. The architecture we are reviewing was designed five years ago, for a business that no longer exists in quite the same shape.

Back then, most of our value sat in two jurisdictions, and the structure reflected that. Since then, the operating footprint has moved — new functions, new counterparties, new risk sitting in places the original design never anticipated. Nothing here is illegal. That is not the question I am asking. The question is whether the structure still describes the company we have actually become.

My concern is drift. When a structure and a business slowly pull apart, no single decision looks wrong, and yet the whole thing stops making sense. So over the next quarter I would like us to document every entity, assess where risk genuinely sits, and challenge the assumptions we inherited rather than defend them out of habit.

And let me be clear about the ambition. I am not looking for something clever. I want an architecture that is boring, defensible, and stable enough to survive the next decade of political change.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to James, why is the board reviewing the architecture now?
options: Because the structure was designed for a business that has since changed shape
Because the structure has been found to be illegal
Because a tax authority has challenged it
items.why: "designed five years ago, for a business that no longer exists in quite the same shape."

items.q: What does James explicitly say is NOT the question he is asking?
items.why: "Nothing here is illegal. That is not the question I am asking."

items.q: What kind of architecture does James say he wants?
items.why: "I want an architecture that is boring, defensible, and stable enough to survive the next decade."

items.q: When James describes "drift," he most likely means that…
options: the structure and the business slowly pulled apart until the whole no longer makes sense
employees have gradually left the tax team
the tax rate has drifted upwards
a single obviously wrong decision was made
items.why: Inferência: "no single decision looks wrong, and yet the whole thing stops making sense" — é o afastamento gradual entre estrutura e negócio.

items.q: What does James's request to "challenge the assumptions we inherited rather than defend them out of habit" suggest about his approach?
options: He blames the previous team for wrongdoing
He wants to preserve the existing structure unchanged
He expects the team to question inherited choices honestly instead of protecting them reflexively
He prefers to delegate the review entirely to advisers
items.why: Inferência: ele pede escrutínio honesto do que foi herdado, não uma defesa automática — postura crítica, não acusatória.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The group's global tax footprint spans eleven jurisdictions." A global tax footprint is…
options: the total tax presence a company has across the countries where it operates
the annual tax bill in the home country
items.why: Global tax footprint = pegada tributária global: a presença fiscal do grupo em todas as jurisdições onde atua.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Once a holding company is established, the arrangement is extremely difficult to ___ without triggering tax charges."
items.why: To unwind = desfazer/desmontar uma estrutura já montada.

items.q: "We decided to base the treasury entity in Ireland." Here, to base an entity means to…
options: locate it there as its home jurisdiction
list it on the stock exchange there
items.why: To base (an entity) = sediar: fixar a jurisdição de domicílio da entidade.

items.q: "The board wanted a structure that was defensible under scrutiny." Defensible means…
options: able to be justified and to withstand challenge
items.why: Defensible = defensável: que se sustenta e se justifica diante de fiscalização ou questionamento.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Under the new design, most of the group's risk will ___ to the entities that actually manage it."
items.why: To flow = fluir: os lucros e o risco "fluem" para determinadas entidades dentro da estrutura.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de conselho sobre estrutura tributária. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the revised architecture." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new entity structure jurisdiction by jurisdiction." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the proposed holding structure." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to review every entity but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, negado, é não concluir.

items.q: "Tidying up the intercompany agreements will not move the needle on the group's overall risk." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível; negado, é não alterar de forma relevante.
